From Birmingham New Street take a local train (10-15 minutes, extra services on matchdays) to Witton, the nearest station to the away turnstiles - turn left out of the station, down to the roundabout, then left into Witton Lane for the away entrance a few minutes' walk away. Aston station is the alternative, about a 10-15 minute walk. Villa also run a matchday express city centre shuttle bus from Dudley Street (near New Street station) to Villa Park, open to home and away fans. Street parking around the ground is residents-only with £60 fines, and a traffic exclusion zone covers Witton Lane and Trinity Road from 2 hours before kick-off to 30-60 minutes after.

From Heathrow take the Piccadilly line direct to Arsenal (about 1 hour 10 minutes); from Gatwick take a train to Victoria then the Victoria line to Highbury & Islington (about 1 hour 15 minutes); from Luton or Stansted take a train to King's Cross St Pancras then the Piccadilly line to Arsenal (about 1 hour).

From Liverpool Lime Street the ground is around two miles away; the club says a taxi from the city centre is usually £8-£10. The 917 Express bus runs from Commutation Row (near Lime Street) in about 15 minutes, and routes 26 (Liverpool ONE), 17 (Queen Square), 68/168, 14 and 19 also stop nearby; a matchday 926 service starts 3.5 hours before kick-off from Liverpool ONE. By Merseyrail, go to Sandhills and take the Soccerbus, which runs from 2 hours before kick-off. Kirkdale is the closest station (just under a mile); Stanley Park car park is permit holders only.

Ten years and three months after Munich, the European Cup. Hibernians of Malta, Sarajevo and Górnik Zabrze were beaten, then Real Madrid in the semi-final: 1–0 at Old Trafford, 3–1 down in the Bernabéu at half-time, then Sadler and Bill Foulkes — Munich survivor, centre-half — scored to go through 4–3. The 12th FA Cup, 12 years after the 11th, and Van Gaal's only trophy — he was sacked two days after the final. Martial, 19, scored the stoppage-time winner against Everton in the semi-final; Marcus Rashford, 18, had burst in with two goals on his debut against Midtjylland in February and two more against Arsenal three days later. The final against Crystal Palace went to extra time after Puncheon's goal and Mata's reply; Lingard volleyed the winner with ten men after Smalling's red card.

The 19th title, the one that passed Liverpool. Unbeaten at home all season, won only five away before February, and still champions by nine points; Chicharito, £7m from Guadalajara, scored 20; Berbatov shared the Golden Boot. Rooney's overhead kick beat City in February; the title was clinched at Blackburn with his penalty on 14 May. The season ended with Barcelona at Wembley — a 3–1 defeat Ferguson called the best side he had faced.
The 20th title. The second goal — Rooney's 40-yard pass, Van Persie's first-time volley — was the Premier League's Goal of the Season.

The Treble. Thirty-three games unbeaten from Boxing Day to the end of May, every competition decided in the final ten days. The league was won on the last day against Tottenham after going a goal down; the FA Cup final against Newcastle was 2–0, four days after the semi-final replay against Arsenal that Schmeichel's penalty save and Giggs's run had turned; and in Barcelona on 26 May, trailing to Mario Basler's sixth-minute free-kick for 85 minutes, Sheringham and Solskjær scored from two Beckham corners in injury time. Keane's semi-final at Juventus — booked, knowing he would miss the final, and dragging United from 2–0 down to win 3–2 — is the performance Ferguson rated above any other.

By public bus: No. 9 from the station to the Transport Museum, then No. 3 from Trinity Street or No. 5 from Pool Meadow to Arena Park (Tesco) and through the underpass. A taxi from the centre is around £15.

The first Double, and nearly a treble — the League Cup final was lost to Aston Villa in March. Roy Keane came from Forest for a British record £3.75m; Cantona was Footballer of the Year. United led the league from August, saw a 16-point gap shrink to three as Blackburn chased, then won six of the last seven. The FA Cup final was 4–0 against Chelsea, who had beaten United twice in the league, with Cantona scoring two penalties in the rain.

The first FA Cup. United beat Brighton, Everton, Blackburn, Burnley and Newcastle on the way to the final at Crystal Palace, where Sandy Turnbull scored the only goal against Bristol City after a Harold Halse shot hit the bar. The same season the club also won the first Charity Shield (1908) and began building Old Trafford, which opened in February 1910.
The first autobiography, written straight after the Treble with McIlvanney — the better of the two for the Govan years, Aberdeen and the building of the first United side.
The first home ground: a field by the railway yard, its lease paid by the railway company. Home until 1893.
The first team moves into the £14 million main building at Carrington in pre-season; the academy building follows in 2002.

The first title in 26 years and the first of the Premier League. United were tenth in November when Eric Cantona arrived from Leeds for £1.2m; they lost twice in the remaining 28 league games. The pivot was 10 April against Sheffield Wednesday: 1–0 down with four minutes left, Bruce headed two, the second in the seventh minute of stoppage time, and Ferguson and Brian Kidd ended up on the pitch. The title was confirmed on 2 May when Villa lost to Oldham; United beat Blackburn the next night and lifted the trophy.

The first title since Munich, taken from Leeds on goal average after both finished on 61 points — the closest finish the division had seen. Law scored 28 in the league and 39 in all competitions and was named European Footballer of the Year; Best, 18, played every league game. The decisive stretch was April: Leeds beaten 1–0 at Elland Road, then seven straight wins.

The first title won at Old Trafford, settled on the last afternoon. United needed to beat Sunderland and hope Villa slipped at Liverpool; they won 5–1 and Villa lost 3–1. Mangnall left for Manchester City the following year, and it would be 41 years before the next championship.

The first trophy in six years, in Ten Hag's first season. Ronaldo left in November after the Piers Morgan interview; Rashford scored 30; Casemiro arrived from Real Madrid and scored the first goal in the final against Newcastle, Sven Botman's own goal the second. The FA Cup final — the first Manchester derby final — was lost 2–1 to City, who went on to the treble.
The flight home from a European Cup quarter-final in Belgrade crashes on take-off at Munich-Riem. 23 die, among them eight players: Bent, Byrne, Colman, Edwards, Jones, Pegg, Taylor and Whelan.
The free school meals campaign — the one time in the post-Ferguson years a United player led the national conversation.
The fresh start gets a new name, with Davies as president; red shirts, white shorts and black socks follow. Club sources give 26 April.
The fuller, later life: Busby's Scottish mining roots, the Manchester City and Liverpool years, and a clear-eyed view of the decline after 1968.
The goal usually credited with saving Ferguson's job.
The goalkeeper of the first great side on Denmark 92, the Treble and why he left a year early.

The largest winning margin in Premier League history at the time — 18 points — with eleven straight wins to finish. United did not defend the FA Cup, going to Brazil for the Club World Championship instead, but in November had beaten Palmeiras in Tokyo to be world champions: Keane scored, Mark Bosnich made the saves. The European Cup went at the quarter-final, 3–2 at home to Real Madrid after a 0–0 in the Bernabéu.
The last of the four sides to be covered after the war.
The listing on the London Stock Exchange raises £6.7 million.
The low point — followed by 6–3 at Southampton and a first home European defeat to Fenerbahçe. United still finished seven clear.

The one major European trophy United had never won, two days after the Manchester Arena attack.
The one player every Busby Babe said was the best of them, dead at 21. Reconstructs the career from match reports and the people who saw him.

The one that kept Ferguson in the job, or so the story goes: United finished 13th and had been out of the top half most of the season. Mark Robins' header at Forest in the third round started a run of away draws all the way to Wembley. The final against Crystal Palace was 3–3, Hughes equalising in extra time; Ferguson dropped Jim Leighton for the replay and Les Sealey kept a clean sheet as Lee Martin's goal won it.
The one with the Haaland tackle and the prawn sandwiches; Dunphy's voice makes it the angriest and most quotable football book of its time.

The point that left Liverpool needing to win at Wimbledon the next night. They lost, Newcastle drew, and the title was United's.
The quiet midfielder on the 2008 side and on depression after the Moscow final — unusually honest for a player book.

Visiting fans are in the Anfield Road Stand (allocation around 3000 for league games) with licensed safe standing in rows 6-35. Enter via gates Q and R, approaching Anfield Road from the 97 Avenue direction; there is no access from Arkles Lane. Turnstiles open 2 hours before kick-off.

Visiting fans are usually held in the stadium for 20 to 30 minutes after the final whistle. For daytime games the Cercanías platform fills quickly after the whistle, so buy a return ticket on arrival.

Visiting supporters are in Blocks 114 to 118 in the north-east corner, lower tier (Block 234 for accessible seating). Approach via Worcester Avenue and use Entrances 11 and 12 (11a is the accessible entrance); there is a security cordon, metal detector and pat-down before the ticket turnstiles.

Visiting supporters are in the corner of the Arthur Wait Stand next to the Whitehorse Lane end (around 2000 places); the away turnstiles are on one side of the Arthur Wait Stand and away fans usually use entrances 4, 5, 6 or 7. Turnstiles open around two hours before kick-off.

How the site works for everyone
manutd.wiki aims to meet the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2 at level AA, on phones and computers, in light and dark mode and in every language the site offers.
The site is built to work with a keyboard: focus is shown with a clear outline, and every page starts with a “Skip to main content” link.
Buttons and links on phones have tap areas of about 44 × 44 pixels where practical.
Text and controls are checked for colour contrast in light and dark mode; you can pick either in the footer, or follow your device.
Pages reflow from wide screens down to phone width without sideways scrolling, and keep their content in a sensible reading order.
Animations are switched off when your device asks for reduced motion.
Ask can be used by voice and can read its answers aloud.

On 7 November 2026, 20 key pages were scanned with an automated WCAG 2.2 A and AA checker (axe-core 4.10) in light and dark mode at 1280 and 390 pixels wide, and the issues it found were fixed. Keyboard use of the header, match actions and navigation was checked by hand, and the layout was reviewed at 375, 390 and 430 pixels wide. The site has not had a full manual audit or testing with screen-reader users, so it does not claim full conformance.
On Trips, a few away fixtures shown in a club’s own colours fall just short of the contrast target (4.47:1 against 4.5:1).
On Who wore this number?, the band of holders puts links inside a scrolling control, and the small dots for each holder are under 24 pixels on phones.
The appearance switch in the footer has small buttons.
Content from other services, such as embedded YouTube videos, the stadium seat map and linked websites, is outside the site’s control.
If something on the site is hard to use, email us with the page and what happened.
